name: Kothu Parotta
cuisine: Tamil Nadu (Madurai-style street food; also eaten in Kerala and Sri Lanka)

ingredients.name: Parotta (Malabar / Kerala style, ready-made or leftover)
Salna (thin spiced gravy served with parotta), warm

equipment: Wide kadai, heavy tawa or flat-bottomed non-stick pan (about 24 cm)
Two flat-edged metal spatulas or one sturdy spatula for chopping (street stalls use a long steel spatula on an iron tawa)
Small bowl and fork for the eggs
Measuring spoons and a kitchen scale (spoon measures are given for the scale-less)

steps.title: Tear the parotta
steps.text: Tear 120 g parotta into pieces about 2 cm wide and put them in a bowl.
steps.tip: Do this first, so the pan is never waiting.
steps.visualCue: A loose pile of flaky, layered pieces with no big chunks left
steps.cameraCheck: The torn parotta pieces in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Hands tearing a parotta into small pieces.
steps.watchOut: Very large pieces that do not take up the masala; keep tearing until nothing is bigger than a 2 cm square. Soft fresh parotta is easier to tear than cold hard parotta; microwave cold parotta for 20 seconds first.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Chop 60 g onion fine.
steps.visualCue: Small even pieces, about 4 mm
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping onion.
steps.watchOut: Uneven pieces, where small bits burn while big bits stay raw; chop to one size.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Chop 60 g tomato fine and keep the juice.
steps.visualCue: Small red pieces with the juice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A tomato being diced.
steps.watchOut: Throwing away the juice, which helps the masala come together; scrape it all in.

steps.title: Chop the chilli
steps.text: Chop 1 green chilli (4 g) fine.
steps.visualCue: Small green rings and bits
steps.videoShot: A knife chopping a green chilli.
steps.watchOut: Touching your eyes after chopping chilli, which burns; wash your hands with soap straight away.

steps.title: Measure the ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Put 8 g (1½ tsp) ginger-garlic paste in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small pale mound of paste with a sharp smell
steps.videoShot: A spoon of paste placed in a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Using old, brown, sour-smelling paste, which tastes harsh; use fresh paste.

steps.title: Mix the powders
steps.text: Mix ½ tsp (1.5 g) chilli powder, ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric and ½ tsp (1 g) garam masala in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: A red-orange powder mix with no white or yellow streaks
steps.videoShot: Powders tapped into a bowl and stirred.
steps.watchOut: Adding the garam masala early to the hot pan, where it loses its smell; keep it ready in this bowl and add all at once in step 15.

steps.title: Beat the eggs
steps.text: Crack 2 eggs into a bowl, add 0.5 g salt (a tiny pinch) and beat with a fork.
steps.visualCue: An even pale-yellow liquid with no clear white strings
steps.videoShot: A fork beating eggs in a bowl.
steps.watchOut: Eggshell in the bowl; fish it out with a clean spoon.

steps.title: Warm the salna
steps.text: Heat 60 ml (4 tbsp) salna in a small pan or microwave until hot.
steps.visualCue: Steam rises and small bubbles appear at the edge
steps.videoShot: Steam rising from a small pan of gravy.
steps.watchOut: Cold salna, which cools the pan and makes the parotta soggy; pour it in only when hot.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the wide pan on medium-high heat and add 10 ml (2 tsp) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmery and ripples when you tilt the pan
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled across a hot pan.
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil, which burns the spices; lower the heat for 20 seconds.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 g (½ tsp) fennel seeds and the 1 cm cinnamon piece.
steps.visualCue: The fennel sizzles and smells sweet, and the cinnamon curls
steps.videoShot: Fennel seeds sizzling in oil.
steps.watchOut: Fennel turning dark brown, which tastes bitter; add the next ingredient at once.

steps.title: Add the leaves and chilli
steps.text: Add 6 curry leaves (3 g) and the chopped green chilli.
steps.visualCue: The leaves crackle and curl and the chilli smell rises
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves crackling in oil.
steps.watchOut: Water drops on the leaves, which make the oil spit; dry the leaves first.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns soft and see-through, then light golden at the edges, and smells sweet
steps.videoShot: Onion turning translucent in the pan.
steps.watchOut: Dark brown edges, which taste bitter; sprinkle 1 tbsp water and lower the heat.

steps.title: Add the ginger-garlic paste
steps.text: Add the paste and stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw sharp smell goes and a warm, savoury smell rises
steps.cameraCheck: The paste cooking with the onion
steps.videoShot: Paste stirred into onion.
steps.watchOut: Paste sticking and browning; add 1 tbsp water and stir.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and cook, mashing it with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The tomato turns soft and pulpy and oil shows at the edges of the masala
steps.videoShot: Tomato mashed to a pulp.
steps.watchOut: Tomato pieces staying firm and watery; cover for 1 minute, then mash again.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Add the mixed powders and 2 tbsp (30 ml) water and stir.
steps.visualCue: A thick red-orange paste with no dry powder left and a spiced smell
steps.videoShot: Powders stirred into masala with a splash of water.
steps.watchOut: Powders scorching in a dry pan, which gives a bitter smell; the water is there to stop that.

steps.title: Scramble in the eggs
steps.text: Pour in the beaten eggs and stir slowly on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The egg sets in soft, small curds that mix into the masala and no longer look runny
steps.cameraCheck: The scrambled egg in the masala
steps.videoShot: Egg setting into curds in the masala.
steps.watchOut: A rubbery dry egg; take it off the heat as soon as it is just set, since it cooks again with the parotta.

steps.title: Add the parotta
steps.text: Add the torn parotta and toss on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: Every piece is coated in the red masala and you can see yellow egg flecks through it
steps.cameraCheck: The coated parotta in the pan
steps.videoShot: Parotta pieces tossed in masala.
steps.watchOut: Pieces at the bottom sticking to the pan; toss from the bottom up with the spatula.

steps.title: Add the salna and salt
steps.text: Pour in the hot salna, add 1 g salt (a pinch) and toss; cook until the liquid is absorbed.
steps.visualCue: The parotta pieces turn soft and darker orange, and the liquid soaks in
steps.cameraCheck: The moist parotta in the pan
steps.videoShot: Salna poured over the parotta.
steps.watchOut: Too much liquid, which makes a mushy paste instead of separate pieces; keep tossing on high heat until the pan looks nearly dry. Too dry and stiff: sprinkle 1 tbsp hot water.

steps.title: Chop and pound
steps.text: Chop and press the mix with the edges of two spatulas (or smash with the edge of a steel katori) in short, quick strokes.
steps.visualCue: The pieces break into smaller, softer shreds, the egg and masala blend through, and you hear a rhythmic metal scraping sound
steps.cameraCheck: The shredded mix in the pan
steps.videoShot: Two spatulas chopping parotta in the pan.
steps.watchOut: Pounding too long, which turns it to paste; stop when the shreds are about 1 cm and still have texture.
steps.funFact: The name comes from the Tamil word "koththu", meaning "to chop", for how it is made on the griddle (Wikipedia, Kottu article, seen in a snippet).

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the 1 g garam masala from the bowl if you kept some aside, 1 tbsp (3 g) chopped coriander leaves, and toss once.
steps.tip: Keep a pinch of garam masala back from step 15 for this step if you like a stronger smell.
steps.visualCue: Bright green flecks through the orange shreds and a warm spiced smell
steps.cameraCheck: The finished kothu in the pan
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the shredded parotta.
steps.watchOut: Cooking after the coriander goes in, which dulls its colour; toss once and switch off.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Tip the kothu (about 300 g) onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Hot, steaming, orange-red shreds with yellow egg and green coriander, slightly moist but not wet
steps.videoShot: A slow pan over the plate.
steps.watchOut: Waiting too long, since it turns stodgy as it cools; eat it hot.

reasons: a decent 24 g of protein from two eggs, but the base is refined-flour (maida) parotta (fibre only about 3.5 g), 34 g of fat, about 9 g of saturated fat, about 375 mg of cholesterol and about 1,200 mg of sodium for one plate. Restaurants use a whole 2-parotta plate on an oily iron tawa with more salna and salt.

researchRating.basis: a very widely published South Indian street classic (Swasthi's, Sailu's Food, Yummy Tummy, Archana's Kitchen, Saffron Trail, Chitra's Food Book, Three Whistles Kitchen and many others), and widely covered in food articles; star counts were not visible (pages seen through snippets only), so the score is a judgement of how widely and warmly it is covered.

storage: Best eaten fresh; the parotta turns stodgy as it cools. If needed, cool within 2 hours and keep in an airtight box in the fridge for 1 day (FitPlate suggestion for a cooked-egg dish, general food-safety practice, not from a recipe source). Not recommended for the freezer (scrambled egg and soft parotta turn watery). Reheat in a hot pan with 1 tbsp water, tossing, until steaming hot all through.
leftoverRemix: Stuff leftover kothu into a toasted bread slice or roti with a slice of cheese for a "kothu toastie" (FitPlate suggestion, not from a source).
burnOff: about 9.7 km of running (680 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 13.6 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 43 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: maida parotta, egg, onion and garlic

ekadashi.reason: wheat flour, egg, onion and garlic

jain.reason: egg, onion, garlic and fresh ginger; a Jain version would be a different dish

ramadan.reason: eggs need no halal sourcing; fine at iftar, but at about 680 kcal (est.) and about 1,200 mg sodium (est.) it is heavy and salty for sehri unless the salt is cut

jain.reason: egg, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root vegetables); Jain rules also exclude egg

vegan.reason: egg; ready parotta and salna commonly also contain milk, ghee or curd (not verified for every brand)

pescatarian.reason: no meat or fish; egg is allowed in a pescatarian diet

glutenFree.reason: parotta is made from wheat flour (maida) and the pan masala may use compounded hing (none is in this recipe)

dairyFree.reason: the recipe adds no dairy, but ready-made parotta and salna may contain milk, ghee or curd; use oil-only parotta and a coconut-based salna (see Diet variants)
